newsitem.title: USA: Grupo Simec in talks to restructure debt.
newsitem.headline: Grupo Simec in talks to restructure debt.

text.p: Mexican steelmaker Grupo Simec SA de CV on Thursday said it entered discussions with its creditors to restructure its debt by lengthening maturities.

As a part of a restructuring proposed by Simec, holders of medium-term notes would be asked to exchange at par the notes due December 12, 1998, for new 10 1/2 percent notes of Simec's Compania Siderurgica de Guadalajara subsidiary, denominated in U.S. dollars and due 2007.
Grupo Simec said principal of the new notes will be repaid in semiannual installments beginning in 1999.
The new notes will not be guaranteed by Grupo Sidek SA de CV, which owns about 28 percent of Simec, Simec said.
Under the restructuring, Simec's Mexican bank creditors will exchange existing debt for new debt of Compania Siderurgica de Guadalajara with longer maturities.
Certain of these creditors also agreed in principle to provide working capital loans to Simec upon successful completion of the restructuring, the company said.
Simec said it expected to distribute to its creditors the terms of the proposed restructuring, including the proposed treatment of each class of debt, by the end of this month.

Simec said it is the only major subsidiary of Grupo Sidek which generates operating profits, and the restructuring of Simec will not serve as a model for the restructuring of the rest of Grupo Sidek and its subsidiaries.
It is anticipated that the shares of Simec held by Grupo Sidek will be sold as part of the restructuring of Grupo Sidek, Simec said.
Holders of the restructured debt of Simec will have a right to redeem their Simec debt at par upon any sale of Simec.
Simec has retained Lehman Brothers as its financial adviser to conduct an exchange of Simec's medium-term notes, which is expected to be made in July.
